problem: Robot navigation stacks rely mostly on metric information and struggle with complex tasks and unexpected situations. They are also tied to specific robot kinematics and to either indoor or outdoor domains.
motivation: Robots need to understand their working environment beyond metric maps to plan tasks and react to unpredictable circumstances. A knowledge-based representation could let robots with different kinematics share one framework across indoor and outdoor large dynamic environments.
key_idea: Use a Triplet Ontological Semantic Model (TOSM) to build a semantic map and semantic knowledge, convert inferred knowledge into PDDL for robot-specific task planning, and maintain the map and re-plan when unexpected situations occur.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract suggests that separating semantic knowledge (TOSM) from robot-specific planning (PDDL conversion) is what allows one framework to serve heterogeneous robots and domains.
method: TOSM-based semantic knowledge: defines a triplet ontological semantic model for environments, objects and robots.
Semantic map generation: builds a semantic map for indoor and outdoor domains from the TOSM knowledge.
Knowledge inference to PDDL: converts inferred knowledge into PDDL so each robot plans according to its own characteristics.
Map maintenance policy: a policy for keeping the semantic map up to date.
Re-planning policy: handles unexpected situations during task execution.

setting.backbone: ontology reasoning + PDDL planner (not a learned model)
setting.action_space: not stated in abstract; PDDL task-level plans executed by robots with different kinematics

results: The abstract reports experiments on four kinds of robots across four scenarios that validate the scalability and reliability of the framework. No quantitative numbers or baselines are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative evaluation and baselines are unknown.
No standard embodied-navigation benchmark evaluation is evident.
